AUTH-001.note: new customer: prove → NAME_REQUIRED → sign-up → session; /me 200

AUTH-003.note: wrong OTP code → 422 PHONE_VERIFICATION_FAILED, no session

AUTH-004.note: OTP expiry is enforced by the MSG91 widget/verifyAccessToken (the server trusts its verdict). Not reachable with PHONE_OTP_DRIVER=fake; verify against MSG91 staging. Server-side: a malformed/expired-shaped token is rejected (see AUTH-003).

AUTH-005.note: server replay guard: same access token reused → 422 "That code has been used" (spent-token counter in CachePort)

AUTH-006.note: OTP attempt cap is MSG91-side. The server adds a per-number sign-in rate limit, tested under ABUSE-001/API-SEC-427 on the rate-limited instance.

AUTH-007.note: OTP resend cap is MSG91-side (widget). Not reachable with the fake driver.

AUTH-008.note: OTP provider outage UX requires a real/forced MSG91 failure; see RECOVERY-448 for the server-side partial-session check with a rejected token.

AUTH-009.note: prove step creates a sign-up ticket, not a user; a refresh before naming leaves no half-made account

AUTH-010.note: concurrent sign-in attempts for distinct numbers both resolve to their own ticket

AUTH-011.note: logout revokes the session (DB revokedAt set); /me → 401 afterwards

AUTH-012.note: Logout-all is not a V1 requirement (product decision confirmed by owner). No route exists; revokeAllForUser is present but unused. Documented as a future consideration, not a defect.

AUTH-013.note: expired session → 401 (graceful; web redirects to login)

AUTH-014.note: cross-customer support ticket read → n/a; A's enquiry list excludes B's

AUTH-015.note: dd_session: HttpOnly ✓, SameSite=Lax ✓, Path=/ ✓, Expires ✓; Secure is set when NODE_ENV=production (code-verified: secure: env.isProduction). Dev response has no Secure, as expected.

CUSTOMER-001.note: customer /me returns name "Account Cust" + masked phone for the account menu/avatar

CUSTOMER-002.note: Saved Cars endpoint reachable by customer

CUSTOMER-003.note: My Enquiries endpoint reachable by customer

CUSTOMER-004.note: after logout: /me → 401, public browsing still 200 (public state restored)

CUSTOMER-005.note: customer account and enquiry history stay usable after the enquiry's dealer is suspended

CUSTOMER-006.note: a customer who accepted a dealer invitation keeps full customer account access (one identity, two seats)

CUSTOMER-007.note: after membership revocation the person's customer account still works

CUSTOMER-008.note: membership revoked: user ACTIVE, CUSTOMER seat untouched, but dealer console → 401 (dealer access gone, customer auth intact)

CUSTOMER-009.note: dealership suspended: member's customer account works (me 200), dealer console 401

CUSTOMER-010.note: Customer and dealership authorization are independent seats, re-read per request; CUSTOMER-005/008/009 demonstrate each stays intact as the other changes.

SAVED-001.note: customer saves an ACTIVE car; it appears in the saved list

SAVED-002.note: unauthenticated save → 401; web wraps this as the login-and-return intent (browser dimension in Agent UAT)

SAVED-004.note: saving twice yields exactly one saved_vehicles row (idempotent PUT)

SAVED-005.note: saved cars persist across logout/login (server-side storage)

SAVED-006.note: a RESERVED car can be saved and shows in its reserved/unavailable group

SAVED-007.note: a SOLD saved car shows as no-longer-available without corrupting the saved list or history

SAVED-008.note: a WITHDRAWN saved car renders as unavailable without error

SAVED-009.note: a saved car whose listing is later withdrawn/removed does not break Saved Cars; saved_vehicles row preserved (R74 never-delete)

SAVED-010.note: saved records are session-scoped (no id in path); another customer sees only their own
